scope: Proposition 11 of the manuscript “Simulating One-Tape Time in Two-Fifths-Power Space” (preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 137 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 873c9e2790a66c53), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a deterministic machine with a fixed number of ordinary writable tapes and read-only input heads, unit movement and fixed origins for all heads, cap-independent symbol functions, and a fixed accessor. For every public input x and supplied binary cap T ≥ 2 satisfying the access condition, its finite-control and halting outcome admits a deterministic simulation in e O( √ T) work-space bits, excluding read-only input storage. Simulation time is unrestricted.
